question: does any held-out or validation figure rest on a scorer or model that read held-out CRISPRi pairs through measured.load_crispri (both files merged) or through the compiled program's `<id>_measured` blocks?
answer: no. Zero consumers are EXPOSED. Every scorer that makes a held-out claim reads the two benchmark files separately through crispri.load and fits on training only. The two defective paths feed only evaluation (measured_layer_genome, confidence_calibration_genome) and reports (evidence census, CLI, explorer, syntax censuses). The held-out links do sit in the compiled programs (43 of 212 measured rules genome-wide, 1 of 2 in the committed chr21 copy), so the defect is latent: the first feature to read a compiled program would have seen the test set.
consequence_for_the_fix: no figure has to change. load_crispri keeps its default (both splits) because no exposed caller exists; each pair now carries its split and the five power columns, and the compiled program marks held-out links so that no feature reads them

status_legend.EXPOSED: a scorer's feature or fit read held-out pairs
status_legend.CLEAN: the scorer and every model it relies on read the splits apart and fit on training only
status_legend.EVALUATION-ONLY: scores against the pairs, fits nothing to them
status_legend.REPORT-ONLY: reads the path for a count, display or syntax only

rows.figures: data/results/measured_layer_genome.json: 19,070 of 440,377 compiled elements measured; CRISPRi agreement over 1,505 matched elements and over the 128 where the predicted gene was tested
rows.why: compares the compiled AlphaGenome predictions with measured outcomes; RECIPROCAL_OVERLAP and the agreement rules are constants, nothing is fitted to the pairs, and the prediction side (enhancer_targets*) never reads CRISPRi. Pooled across splits by design; not quoted as a held-out figure

rows.figures: data/results/confidence_calibration_genome.json: 128 tested elements, observed 0.758 against stated 0.347; stated level outside its interval in 10 of 12 bands
rows.why: a reliability table: CONFIDENCE_BANDS imported unchanged from target_calibration (fixed 2026-09-17), the confidence formula is compile.py's clipped |log2FC|; no parameter is fitted on the measured pairs

rows.figures: 212 measured rules in the 24 compiled programs, 43 of them held-out-only links; the committed chr21 copy carries 2 rules, 1 held-out-only (ICOSLG, GM12878)
rows.why: the held-out links are in the program, but no scorer, fit or feature reads a compiled program: its readers are evidence.py (fact census), cli `measured-layer` (prints the JSON), the web explorer index, `bio test` on the program's own `# test:` lines, and three syntax censuses (biolang_key_census, mandatory_locations, amounts_or_concentrations)

rows.why: counts evidence kinds; reads no label as a feature

rows.path: crispri.load of both files, not load_crispri
rows.figures: data/results/node_containment_measured.json: 661 regulated pairs (K562 589, HCT116 34, GM12878 16, WTC11 15, Jurkat 7), measured share 0.758
rows.why: the regulated pairs are the ground truth the node caller is scored against; nodes come from CTCF cCREs and GENCODE, nothing is fitted to a pair. Merging the splits is legitimate here because no model is trained, and the figure is not quoted as held-out

rows.path: own CRISPRI_FILES tuples, both files, intervals only
rows.why: read tested intervals as a coverage footprint; no label is read

overlap_reading: 0 identical pairs, but 249 of 4,378 held-out pairs share at least one base with a training interval: 36 on the same gene (4 near-identical, 32 overlapping; HCT116 23, WTC11 13) and 213 on another gene (K562 164). No held-out K562 pair repeats a training gene at an overlapping interval. crispri.score already reports an arm on held-out elements not in training (heldout_elements_not_in_training); every other held-out figure includes the related pairs
reused_benchmark: the held-out file has been read by at least ten scored results (crispri_benchmark, crispri_contact, crispri_published, crispri_direction, crispri_direction_both, target_calibration, target_calibration_gate, target_prevalence, target_rebanding, union_axis, and loci_fourth/loci_noncoding for its held-out arm). Each registration froze its model before its own read, but the choices between registrations were made by people who had seen the earlier reads, so every figure on it is reported as a reused benchmark and not as a first touch
r5_provenance: every CrispriPair now carries split (partition), source_file, assay and study (the Dataset column), frozen at parse time; measured.development_only raises on a held-out pair; measured.split_overlap is the automated overlap check, and tests/test_crispri_split.py recomputes it against this file
variants: not applicable to CRISPRi: the benchmark tests intervals, not alleles, so the related-variant half of the overlap check has nothing to compare

figures_changed.compiled_programs: held-out-only links (43 genome-wide, 1 in the committed chr21 copy) keep their rule but leave `targets:` and carry measured.HELDOUT_MARK; 1 training-supported rule genome-wide took its strength from a held-out pair and now takes it from the training pair; rule, entity and unknown counts unchanged

r2_outcomes.rule: a pair is significant_decrease, significant_increase, not_significant_well_powered (PowerAtEffectSize20 >= 0.8), not_significant_underpowered, or missing; ValidConnection FALSE rows are counted as invalid and never read. Only a well-powered null may disagree; an increase is its own verdict and raises no rule
r2_outcomes.why_20pct: PowerAtEffectSize25 is >= 0.8 on every non-significant pair in both files (the benchmark's own filter), so it cannot separate; 20% is the column genomeos-8a's brief counted (6,169 of 9,810)
